# Benchmark results — vx vs Turborepo vs Nx

<!-- Generated by `bun bench/compare.ts`. Do not edit by hand. -->

- **Workspace:** 300 packages, 10 dependency layers, ~3 deps/package, 2 tasks (build + test).
- **Tasks:** `build` = `mkdir -p dist && : > dist/out.txt`; `test` = `true` — identical across all runners.
- **Measured:** whole-repo `build`+`test`, median of 2, wall-clock of the CLI invocation.
- **Concurrency:** 10 (pinned identically for every runner).
- **Host:** Linux 6.18.5 · 4 cores · linux/x64
- **Date:** 2026-06-13

| Runner      | Version  | Fresh (cold)     | Warm (no restore) | Warm (restore)   |
| ----------- | -------- | ---------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| vx          | vx 0.0.0 | 2.45 s           | 339 ms            | 391 ms           |
| vx (frozen) | vx 0.0.0 | 1.88 s (0.8× vx) | 298 ms (0.9× vx)  | 422 ms (1.1× vx) |
| turbo       | 2.9.18   | 1.72 s (0.7× vx) | 335 ms (1.0× vx)  | 436 ms (1.1× vx) |
| nx          | 22.7.5   | 8.73 s (3.6× vx) | 2.16 s (6.4× vx)  | 2.08 s (5.3× vx) |

**Cache states.** _Fresh_ clears the runner's cache and runs cold (key
derivation + execution + save). _Warm, no restore_ re-runs with the cache
warm and outputs intact (the steady-state dev loop). _Warm, restore_
deletes every `dist/` first, so the runner restores outputs from cache.

Reproduce: `bun bench/compare.ts 300 10 2`.
